items.question: How safe is the United States?
items.answer:
It varies enormously by city and neighbourhood. We generally felt comfortable in the places we lived and travelled, but the US is too large for a country-wide safety verdict to be useful.

Use the same judgement you would in any major city, pay attention to neighbourhood-level advice and remember that a place feeling orderly does not mean every area is equally comfortable late at night.

items.question: Is English commonly understood?
items.answer: Yes. If you speak English, language will be among the easiest parts of the trip.

items.question: What could ruin my stay in the United States?
items.answer:
Underestimating distance.

A destination being in the same state does not mean it is nearby. Los Angeles alone can consume hours of driving, and the country as a whole rewards itineraries built by region rather than by a list of famous names.

The second trap is assuming systems will bend for you. America works beautifully when you follow the process. Miss a deadline, a flight cut-off or a reservation rule and you may discover just how efficiently it can tell you no.
